story: Sita was found in a furrow of earth by King Janaka while he was ploughing, so she is called the daughter of the earth. She married Rama, followed him into exile, and was abducted by Ravana. For months in Lanka she refused him, until Rama rescued her.
belief: Sita is seen as an avatar of Lakshmi and the ideal of strength, loyalty and endurance. She is especially loved in Mithila, her homeland, and many women read her story as both an example and a warning.
turns: She asked Rama to chase the golden deer, which was a trap. She stepped over the protective line Lakshmana drew to give alms to a disguised Ravana. After being asked to prove herself again and again, she finally asked the earth to take her back.
facts: She raised her twin sons, Luv and Kush, in Valmiki's hermitage.
Sitamarhi in Bihar and Janakpur in Nepal both claim to be her birthplace.
'Lakshmana rekha' is still a common phrase for a line you must not cross.
